a99c4dda-0665-425e-941a-d55a7fd219b8.title: Monitoring Operating System
a99c4dda-0665-425e-941a-d55a7fd219b8.original_text: The Operator is already logged in. The Operator requests to view the status of a monitoring location. If an Emergency situation occurs then System displays emergency warning message to operator. The system displays the monitoring status as follows: Sensor status for each sensor (value, upper limit, lower limit, alarm status). Monitoring status has been displayed. The Operator is logged in before starting the process. The Operator requests to view the outstanding alarms. If an Emergency situation occurs then System displays emergency warning message to operator. The system displays the outstanding alarms. For each alarm, the system displays the name of the alarm, alarm description, location of alarm, severity of alarm (high, medium, low). Outstanding alarms have been displayed. The remote system is operational in advance. The sensors sends new monitoring data to the system. If an Emergency situation occurs then System displays emergency warning message to operator. The system updates the monitoring status as follows: Sensor status for each sensor (value, upper limit, lower limit, alarm status). The system sends new monitoring status to Monitoring-Operators who have subscribed to receive status updates. Monitoring status has been updated. If an alarm condition is detected then an alarm is generated. Operators are notified of new alarms to which they have subscribed. If Emergency situation is detected then System displays emergency warning message to operator. The external sensor is operational already. The Remote Sensor sends an alarm to the system. If the alarm is severe then a display with flashing warning is done. The system updates the alarm data. The system stores the name of the alarm, alarm description, location of alarm, severity of alarm (high, medium, low). Alarm data have been updated. If the Operator is stuck somewhere in the process then he has an option to use help facility provided by the system. The Monitoring-Operator chooses help facility option. Screen displays a message asking the type of help he wants. Depending on the selection, the system helps him in proceeding with the system.

ai_result.snl_text:
**Actors Identified:**  
- Operator  
- Monitoring-Operator  
- Remote Sensor  
- System (implicit)  

---

**Structured Natural Language (SNL) Requirements:**

1. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to request the status of a monitoring location.
2. The system shall be able to display the status of a monitoring location upon request.
3. The system shall display the sensor status for each sensor at the monitoring location.
4. The system shall display the current value for each sensor.
5. The system shall display the upper limit for each sensor.
6. The system shall display the lower limit for each sensor.
7. The system shall display the alarm status for each sensor.
8. If an emergency situation occurs while the Operator is viewing monitoring status, then the system shall be able to display an emergency warning message to the Operator.
9. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to request to view outstanding alarms.
10. The system shall be able to display all outstanding alarms upon request.
11. For each outstanding alarm, the system shall display the name of the alarm.
12. For each outstanding alarm, the system shall display the description of the alarm.
13. For each outstanding alarm, the system shall display the location of the alarm.
14. For each outstanding alarm, the system shall display the severity of the alarm (high, medium, low).
15. If an emergency situation occurs while the Operator is viewing outstanding alarms, then the system shall be able to display an emergency warning message to the Operator.
16. The system shall be able to receive new monitoring data from sensors.
17. The system shall be able to update the monitoring status upon receiving new monitoring data.
18. The system shall update the sensor status for each sensor with the latest value.
19. The system shall update the upper limit for each sensor as per the new data.
20. The system shall update the lower limit for each sensor as per the new data.
21. The system shall update the alarm status for each sensor as per the new data.
22. If an emergency situation occurs while updating monitoring status, then the system shall be able to display an emergency warning message to the Operator.
23. The system shall be able to send the updated monitoring status to Monitoring-Operators who have subscribed to receive status updates.
24. The system shall provide Monitoring-Operators with the ability to subscribe to receive status updates.
25. The system shall notify Monitoring-Operators of new monitoring status updates to which they have subscribed.
26. The system shall be able to detect alarm conditions based on sensor data.
27. If an alarm condition is detected, then the system shall be able to generate an alarm.
28. The system shall notify Operators of new alarms to which they have subscribed.
29. The system shall provide Operators with the ability to subscribe to alarm notifications.
30. If an emergency situation is detected during alarm generation, then the system shall be able to display an emergency warning message to the Operator.
31. The system shall be able to receive alarms from external Remote Sensors.
32. If the received alarm from a Remote Sensor is severe, then the system shall display a flashing warning message.
33. The system shall be able to update alarm data upon receiving a new alarm.
34. The system shall store the name of the alarm for each new alarm.
35. The system shall store the description of the alarm for each new alarm.
36. The system shall store the location of the alarm for each new alarm.
37. The system shall store the severity of the alarm (high, medium, low) for each new alarm.
38. The system shall be able to update existing alarm data when new information is received.
39. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to access a help facility at any point in the process.
40. The system shall provide the Monitoring-Operator with the ability to choose the help facility option.
41. When the help facility is accessed, the system shall display a message asking the type of help required.
42. The system shall provide the Operator with a list of help topics or options to choose from.
43. The system shall be able to process the Operator’s selection of help type.
44. Depending on the help type selected, the system shall provide guidance to the Operator to proceed with the system.
45. The system shall validate that the Operator is logged in before allowing access to monitoring status.
46. The system shall validate that the Operator is logged in before allowing access to outstanding alarms.
47. The system shall validate that the Operator is logged in before allowing access to the help facility.
48. The system shall validate the integrity of monitoring data received from sensors.
49. If monitoring data from a sensor is invalid or corrupted, then the system shall display an error message to the Operator.
50. The system shall log all emergency warning messages displayed to Operators.
51. The system shall log all alarm notifications sent to Operators.
52. The system shall log all status updates sent to Monitoring-Operators.
53. The system shall provide feedback to the Operator when monitoring status has been successfully displayed.
54. The system shall provide feedback to the Operator when outstanding alarms have been successfully displayed.
55. The system shall provide feedback to the Operator when help facility guidance has been provided.
56. The system shall provide feedback to Monitoring-Operators when monitoring status updates have been sent.
57. The system shall provide feedback to Operators when alarm notifications have been sent.
58. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to acknowledge receipt of emergency warning messages.
59. The system shall record the Operator’s acknowledgment of emergency warning messages.
60. The system shall allow Operators to filter outstanding alarms by severity.
61. The system shall allow Operators to filter outstanding alarms by location.
62. The system shall allow Operators to sort outstanding alarms by time of occurrence.
63. The system shall display a timestamp for each outstanding alarm.
64. The system shall validate that all required fields (name, description, location, severity) are present when storing alarm data.
65. If any required alarm data field is missing, then the system shall display an error message and prevent storage.
66. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to refresh the monitoring status display.
67. The system shall automatically refresh the monitoring status display when new data is received.
68. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to refresh the outstanding alarms display.
69. The system shall automatically refresh the outstanding alarms display when new alarms are generated.
70. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to view details of a specific alarm from the outstanding alarms list.
71. The system shall display detailed information (name, description, location, severity, timestamp) for a selected alarm.
72. The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to return to the main menu from any screen.
73. The system shall prevent unauthorized users from accessing monitoring status, outstanding alarms, or help facility.
74. The system shall provide clear error messages for unauthorized access attempts.
75. The system shall maintain an audit trail of all Operator actions related to monitoring status, alarms, and help facility usage.

items.requirement: The remote system is operational in advance.
items.reason: The AI requirements do not mention that the remote system must be operational before monitoring or alarm processes begin. This is important for system readiness and reliability.

missing_in_ai.description: Requirements from original case study that AI failed to capture

items.requirement: The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to access a help facility at any point in the process.
items.reason: The original case study does not mention a help facility or related user assistance features. Including detailed help system requirements adds unnecessary scope.

items.requirement: The system shall validate the integrity of monitoring data received from sensors.
items.reason: The original case study does not specify data integrity validation or error handling for corrupted data. This is a design/implementation detail not present in the initial requirements.

items.requirement: The system shall log all emergency warning messages displayed to Operators.
items.reason: Logging of messages and actions is not mentioned in the original case study. This is an implementation detail that may not be required at the requirements level.

items.requirement: The system shall allow Operators to filter outstanding alarms by severity.
items.reason: Filtering and sorting alarms by severity, location, or time is not specified in the original requirements. These are advanced UI features that go beyond the initial scope.

items.requirement: The system shall provide the Operator with the ability to acknowledge receipt of emergency warning messages.
items.reason: Acknowledgment of emergency messages is not mentioned in the original case study. This adds complexity and may not be necessary.

overspecified_in_ai.description: Requirements where AI was too detailed or specific beyond case study scope

items.requirement: The system shall update the upper limit for each sensor as per the new data.
items.reason: Sensor upper and lower limits are typically configuration parameters, not values that change with each new data reading. The original case study only mentions displaying these limits, not updating them with each new data point.

items.requirement: The system shall update the lower limit for each sensor as per the new data.
items.reason: As above, lower limits are not updated with each sensor reading. This misinterprets the original requirement.

items.requirement: The system shall provide Monitoring-Operators with the ability to subscribe to receive status updates.
items.reason: The original case study states that Monitoring-Operators who have subscribed receive updates, but does not specify that the system must provide a subscription management feature.

items.requirement: The system shall provide Operators with the ability to subscribe to alarm notifications.
items.reason: As above, the original case study assumes subscriptions exist but does not require the system to provide subscription management.

incorrect_in_ai.description: Requirements where AI made factual errors or misinterpretations

detailed_ai_analysis.analysis_summary: The AI-generated requirements capture most of the core functionality from the original case study but add many extra details not present in the initial requirements, such as help facilities, data validation, logging, filtering, and acknowledgment features. Some requirements misinterpret the original intent, particularly regarding sensor limit updates and subscription management. Only one original requirement (remote system operational in advance) is missing. The AI output is thorough but risks scope creep and implementation bias.
